instruction:
Export the opened two-part character and generate maps from its existing geometry, UVs, normals, and vertex color. Open ZBrush 2025 from the desktop shortcut and continue from `Character.obj`. The input has Head and Body object/groups with UV coordinates and MRGB-style vertex colors; it does not represent a separate high-detail/low-detail bake pair. Preserve those two parts in `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Character.obj`. Use Multi Map Exporter on the current surfaces to produce UV-space `Normal.png`, `Displacement.png`, and `Cavity.png` in `C:\Users\user\Desktop`.

All maps must be 2048 x 2048. Normal.png must be RGB tangent-space data with mean blue channel above 0.5. Displacement.png must be at least 16-bit grayscale, contain at least 1,000 distinct values, and have mean within 0.2 of mid-gray. Cavity.png must be grayscale with at least 50% nonzero pixels. Character.obj must preserve exactly the Head and Body groups, UVs, and nonzero vertex colors.

command:
import ctypes, time
user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
EnumWindowsProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
EnumChildProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
def close_error():
    wins = []
    def wcb(hwnd, lparam):
        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(512)
        user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, 512)
        if 'ZHomePage.exe' in buf.value and 'System Error' in buf.value:
            wins.append(hwnd)
        return True
    user32.EnumWindows(EnumWindowsProc(wcb), 0)
    for hwnd in wins:
        buttons = []
        def ccb(ch, lparam):
            text = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            cls = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            user32.GetWindowTextW(ch, text, 128)
            user32.GetClassNameW(ch, cls, 128)
            if text.value == 'OK' or cls.value == 'Button':
                buttons.append(ch)
            return True
        user32.EnumChildWindows(hwnd, EnumChildProc(ccb), 0)
        for ch in buttons:
            user32.SendMessageW(ch, 0x00F5, 0, 0)
time.sleep(95)
for _ in range(4):
    close_error()
    time.sleep(2)
